item.title: Trump says historic summit with Xi, Putin already a 'win' before event
item.description:
By Jarrett Renshaw and Trevor Hunnicutt

SHENZHEN, China, Nov 19 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump said his meeting on Thursday with Chinese and Russian counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin was already a "win" before it took place, as China gave him a lavish welcome filled with fanfare and pageantry.

The unprecedented diplomatic gathering of the leaders of the world's largest nuclear powers is unlikely to produce major agreements, analysts say, while it unnerves smaller countries that fear their interests might be disregarded.

item.title: China's Xi to host historic summit with Trump, Putin
item.description:
The presidents of China, the United States and Russia posed for a photo with other Asia-Pacific leaders on Thursday ahead of their first trilateral summit, billed by Beijing as talks about "world peace".

The three-way meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen comes with Russia's bloody offensive in Ukraine approaching the five-year mark.

item.title: China's used phones find new homes from Karachi to Algiers
item.description:
In the maze of Shenzhen's neon-lit Huaqiangbei electronics market, buyers from Africa to Bangladesh buy dozens of used phones at a time -- even with cracked screens -- to sell back home.

"From all China, the broken mobile phones come here," Akhtar Muhammad, 38, a Pakistani businessman, told AFP as he browsed the stacks of devices in the southern Chinese city.

"We will fix them in Pakistan."

item.title: Saudi crown prince meets US CENTCOM chief amid escalating Houthi hostilities
item.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper in Riyadh, Cooper's third publicly reported visit to Saudi Arabia since hostilities between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis reignited in July.

The two discussed bilateral relations, particularly regarding military affairs, as well as regional developments, the Saudi state news agency SPA reported on Thursday.

item.title: Top UN court to rule on alleged genocide of Myanmar's Rohingya
item.description:
By Anthony Deutsch and Stephanie van den Berg

THE HAGUE, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The United Nations' highest court hands down a long-awaited judgment on Thursday in a case accusing Myanmar of committing genocide against the minority Rohingya population.

InBangladesh, the 1.2 million Rohingya stuck in the sprawling Cox'sBazar refugee settlement since fleeing widespread violence in 2017 will be following the judgment, set to be read from 10 a.m. (0900 GMT) for up to 90 minutes.

item.title: US sanctions Hezbollah-linked charity in push against Iran's proxies, Treasury says
item.description:
By Andrea Shalal

Nov 18 (Reuters) - The United States on Wednesday issued new Hezbollah-related sanctions targeting three people based in Lebanon, and three entities as part of a broader effort to shut down Iran's proxy networks, the Treasury Department said.

Treasury said its Office of Foreign Assets Control designated the Hezbollah-affiliated charity Ta’awanu Association and its founder, along with two Lebanese brothers who the US said have aided the Islamic militant group with a gold- and cash-smuggling network.

item.title: US sanctions Hezbollah-linked charity in bid to squeeze Iran
item.description: Also sanctioned were members of a gold and cash smuggling network run by Hezbollah and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
